messages:
maya: Quick share — ran the KV-cache prefetch + eviction noise sweep across us-west1 (H100) and eu-north1 (A100) yesterday. attaching a shared drive link with charts. :eyes:
arturo: link? can you drop the command or config you used? want to reproduce.
maya: sure — command was: `./run_kvbench --model redwood-v2-small --seqlen-distributions=prod_trace.json --prefetch=window:32 --evict_policy=lru-window --kernel_hint=auto --quant=fp16`
sasha: nice. did you test with int8/qat variants? cache behavior often changes with quant due to token packing.
maya: did a quick int8 run later: hit-rate similar but tail latency worse on eu. suspect kernel fallback on a100 for int8 path.
owen: eu had higher eviction churn? was the seqlen mix skewed to >1024?
maya: yes — the simulated trace had a long-tail — ~12% of requests >1200. on eu A100 we saw eviction rate spike at that bucket which correlated with p99 jumps.
dana: any quality regressions flagged on the int8 run? rounding/pop artifacts?
maya: ran the eval harness on 50 prompt seeds — tiny delta in generation length (<0.5%) and some sticky stop-token diffs, but nothing that flagged our threshold. still need a larger eval.
arturo: kernel_hint=auto might pick a fallback kernel for long seqlen/int8 on a100; can you try `--kernel_hint=prefer-cutlass` and `--kernel_hint=triton-ff` to compare?
maya: will run both. initial numbers: us-west H100 p50/p95/p99 tokens/ms improved with prefetch, p99 down ~18% but throughput dropped ~6% at 512 batch due to more CPU prefetch ops. eu A100 p99 stayed same or worse with prefetch.
benchmark-bot: Snapshot uploaded: gs://redwood-bench/kvcache/2039987654/plots_v1.png
maya: posted heatmap: hit-rate vs p99 by seqlen bucket. key callouts:
- bucket <256: prefetch wins, hit-rate +12%, p99 -22%
- 256-512: neutral to slight win H100, A100 noisy
- >1024: eviction thrash on eu -> p99 +40% with prefetch on A100 (bad)
arturo: sounds like regional kernel mismatch + memory allocator fragmentation. maybe our pager pagesize differs across regions?
sasha: also check KV cache window size. 32 might be too small for long-tails; try window 64/128 and adaptive window where we increase prefetch window for sequences where we see repeated tokens.
maya: tried window 64 on H100 -> slightly better throughput and p99; on A100 window64 traded better but still had spikes.
dana: could this be due to different driver/runtime versions in eu? we recently rolled CUDA 12.2 -> 12.3 in eu.
own: infra-bot, can you confirm driver/runtime matrix for the two clusters?
infra-bot: us-west1 H100 nodes: CUDA 12.3, driver 535.x, kernel modules 1.2. eu-north1 A100 nodes: CUDA 12.2, driver 525.x.
arturo: aha — different CUDA versions could change which kernels get chosen. that explains fallback on int8 path on A100.
sasha: workaround: pin kernel to a known good path with `--kernel_hint=force-cutlass-int8` and measure. if that fixes tail, we can add region-specific kernel overrides until we standardize runtime.
maya: ran force-cutlass-int8 on eu: p99 improved by ~25% vs auto int8, hit-rate unchanged. throughput ~+3%.
dana: good. what's the plan for model onboard (redwood-v2-small) quantization? do we promote int8?
arturo: promote cautiously — need full eval sweep for generation quality and perf across regions. Also add kernel overrides in config for eu until infra upgrades.
benchmark-bot: Regression check: int8-vs-fp16 quality delta summary uploaded: gs://redwood-bench/kvcache/2039987654/quality_int8_v_fp16.csv
maya: next steps I propose:
- run full eval (2k prompts) for int8 vs fp16 across both regions
- sweep prefetch windows [32,64,128,adaptive] with eviction policies [lru-window, freq, hybrid]
- try kernel hints [auto, prefer-cutlass, force-cutlass-int8, triton-ff]
- coordinate with infra to align CUDA/runtime in eu
arturo: +1. i'll own the kernel hint sweeps and infra coordination.
sasha: i'll prototype an adaptive prefetcher that grows window on repeated KV hits in last N requests.
dana: i'll queue a larger-quality-run and watch for regressions.
own: I'll schedule a quick sync Thurs 10am PT. :calendar:
maya: thanks everyone. leaving the raw logs in the shared drive. I'll post a follow-up thread with consolidated tables once sweeps finish. :thumbsup:
